## Natural history notes

A tiny gall midge characterized by a delicate fly-like adult body, long legs, and narrow wings, though it is much more often noticed by the gall it forms than by the adult insect itself. In Florida, Arnoldiola atra is associated with live oak, where it forms detachable brown to green, leafy or spiky rosette-like galls on buds or stems, especially in spring. The larva develops protected inside the gall, feeding on plant tissue while the gall provides shelter; like many oak gall insects, it also supports a specialized community of parasitoids and other gall-associated insects.
